license_note: Dimensional facts from ASME B1.20.1-2013 (Pipe Threads, General Purpose, Inch), Table 1 and its defining formulas. Standards tables are facts, not copyrightable expression; cite the standard. Tap-drill sizes are trade-published values (Machinery's Handbook and drill-chart consensus). L4 cross-checked against BOSL2 (BSD-2-Clause) threading.scad. Minimum boss OD, tapped depth, blind drill depth, chamfer, fitting hex and metric drill equivalents are engineering rules of thumb, not from any standard.

columns.nominal: nominal pipe size (NPS) -- NOT the thread OD
columns.thread_designation: as marked on drawings, e.g. 1/4-18 NPT
columns.is_nps_pipe_size: true if an ASME B36.10 pipe of this NPS exists; false for 1/16, which is a fitting-only thread
columns.od_in: D, outside diameter of pipe = nominal thread major diameter, inches (ASME B1.20.1 Table 1). On the taper the actual major diameter varies along the length (at the small end it is about E0 + h); do NOT use D as a fit or clearance dimension at the gauge plane
columns.taper: taper, as the standard states it: 1:16 on diameter (3/4 in per foot on diameter, 1/32 per side)
columns.taper_in_per_in_on_dia: diameter change per unit axial length = 0.0625
columns.taper_half_angle_deg: taper angle per side relative to the axis = atan(1/32) = 1.7899 deg
columns.thread_height_h_in: h, truncated thread height = 0.800p, inches (standard's symbol is lower-case h; upper-case H is the sharp-V height)
columns.sharp_v_height_H_in: H, sharp-V thread height = 0.866025p, inches (nomenclature only; the cut thread height is h)
columns.e0_pd_small_end_in: E0, pitch diameter at the small end (start) of the external thread, inches = D - (0.05D + 1.1)p
columns.e1_pd_handtight_plane_in: E1, pitch diameter at the hand-tight (L1 gauge) plane, inches = E0 + 0.0625 L1. This is the pitch diameter at the face of the internal thread (port face) when gauged flush
columns.e2_pd_effective_end_in: E2, pitch diameter at the end of the effective external thread L2, inches = E0 + 0.0625 L2
columns.k0_minor_dia_small_end_in: K0, basic minor diameter at the small end of the external thread, inches = E0 - h. Lathe / single-point programmers: the internal thread bore at its small end (L2 plane of the port) is nominally K0; the tap drill is deliberately larger than K0
columns.l1_handtight_in: L1, hand-tight engagement length between external and internal thread, inches (Table 1)
columns.l1_handtight_threads: L1 in threads = L1 x n
columns.l2_effective_in: L2, effective (full-form) external thread length, inches = (0.8D + 6.8)p (Table 1). DESIGN THE PORT THREAD LENGTH TO L2, not to L1 + L3
columns.l3_wrench_makeup_in: L3, wrench make-up length for the internal thread = 3p, inches
columns.l3_wrench_makeup_mm: L3 in mm (25.4 x the rounded inch value, per this table's stated convention; differs from 25.4 x 3/n by <= 0.001 mm)
columns.v_vanish_in: V, vanish (incomplete, chamfer-cone) thread length = 3.47p, inches, as tabulated by the standard (for 14 tpi the standard's rounding gives 0.2478, consistent with its L4)
columns.l4_ext_thread_length_in: L4, overall length of external thread = L2 + V (NOT L2 + L3), inches (Table 1)
columns.l5_nominal_perfect_ext_in: L5, nominal length of perfect external threads = L2 + L3, inches (Table 1)
columns.tap_drill: common UNREAMED tap drill name (letter / fractional) for tapping straight from the drill; see tap_drill_alternatives for the sizes other charts give
columns.tap_drill_mm: unreamed tap drill diameter, mm (inch x 25.4, half-up to 3 dp)
columns.tap_drill_reamed: drill to use BEFORE an NPT taper reamer (drill-then-ream practice); do not use this drill without the reamer
columns.tap_drill_alternatives: other drill sizes published for this size, so a student can recognise them on a generic chart; text
columns.tap_drill_metric_nearest: RECALL -- nearest stock metric drills for shops without letter/64ths drills, with over/under note; text. A slightly SMALL drill means more tap torque and a deeper-seating fitting; a slightly LARGE drill means fewer full threads and the fitting seats further in -- prefer the size nearest the inch drill and gauge the finished port
columns.gauge_check: how the finished port is accepted: L1 plug gauge hand-tight flush with port face +/- 1 turn (ASME B1.20.1 gauging). Run the tap in stages and gauge; do NOT tap to the tap's shoulder
columns.min_tapped_depth_mm: RECALL rule of thumb -- suggested minimum full-thread depth for a BLIND port = L2 + 2p, mm. Not from the standard. Drill deeper still: see blind_drill_depth_* columns
columns.min_boss_height_through_port_mm: RECALL rule of thumb -- for a THROUGH port (tank end cap, bulkhead) the same value applies as the minimum material thickness at the port along the thread axis (boss height / end-cap thickness) = L2 + 2p, mm, plus any chamfer
columns.blind_drill_depth_full_dia_mm: RECALL rule of thumb -- drill depth at full diameter for a blind port = min_tapped_depth + tap chamfer lead (3.5 threads, the long end of the 2-3.5 thread taper-chamfer range), rounded up to 0.5 mm. Model the hole in CAD to this depth
columns.blind_drill_depth_to_point_mm: RECALL rule of thumb -- depth to the 118 deg drill point tip = blind_drill_depth_full_dia + 0.3 x drill dia, rounded up to 0.5 mm; the minimum floor material must be measured from here
columns.port_chamfer_dia_mm: RECALL shop practice -- 90 deg countersink (or shallow spot face) diameter at the port mouth = od_mm + 1.0 mm, so the first thread is not pushed proud and the fitting/wrench sees a flat face
columns.typical_fitting_hex_af: RECALL, vendor dependent -- typical across-flats hex of a male NPT adapter of this size; across-corners = AF x 1.155. Boss OD and spot face must clear the wrench; check the actual fitting drawing
columns.min_boss_od_in: RECALL rule of thumb -- minimum outside diameter of material to leave around a tapped port, roughly 1.65-2x pipe OD (about 0.35-0.5x pipe OD of wall per side), inches. Not from any standard; not a checked pressure-vessel minimum; for a pressurised boss it must be replaced by a hoop-stress / burst calculation
columns.min_boss_od_ratio_to_od: min_boss_od / pipe OD, for transparency about the rule of thumb
columns.min_boss_od_confidence: confidence for the boss column alone (always recall)
columns.remark: row-specific caution, present only where needed
columns.disputed: present only where published charts disagree: {field: [alternatives with source]}; the row keeps the Machinery's Handbook value
columns.tap_drill_confidence: present only on rows with a disputed tap drill: confidence for the tap_drill value alone
columns.tap_drill_reamed_confidence: present only where the reamed drill is recall rather than chart-confirmed
columns.confidence: row-level confidence = the LOWEST confidence among the standard-derived fields (OD, tpi, L*, E*, K0). Fields marked RECALL in their column description carry 'recall' regardless of this value; see field_confidence
columns.source: standard / document each group of values comes from

rows.tap_drill_alternatives: D (0.246) unreamed per Machinery's Handbook; C (0.242) with reamer; some charts give 1/4 (0.250) -- treat as disputed
rows.gauge_check: L1 plug gauge (or fitting) hand-tight flush with port face, tolerance +/- 1 turn; tap depth, not drill size, sets this
rows.remark: NOT an NPS pipe size: no ASME B36.10 pipe exists at 1/16; fitting-only thread (gauges, small instrument fittings). Use 1/8 NPT unless a specific fitting demands 1/16.

notes: 1) DO NOT MODEL THE TAPER. Model the port as a plain hole at tap_drill diameter, to blind_drill_depth_full_dia_mm for a blind port (or through, for a through port), attach a cosmetic thread / hole-wizard NPT feature so CAM and inspection do not read it as a plain drilled hole, and call out the thread on the drawing (e.g. '1/4-18 NPT, gauge L1 plug flush +/-1 turn'). The 1:16 taper (1.7899 deg per side) is cut by the tap. Only model the tapered thread if single-point threading on a lathe, and then use the E0/E1/E2/K0 columns of this table (re-derived from the standard's formulas) and confirm against ASME B1.20.1 Table 1 before cutting. 2) NPS is not the OD. '1/4 NPT' has a 0.540 in (13.716 mm) nominal major diameter; the tap drill (7/16 = 11.113 mm) is what you cut. 1/16 NPT is not a pipe size at all (no B36.10 pipe exists); it is a fitting-only thread. 3) TAP DEPTH SETS THE PORT, NOT DRILL SIZE. Tap in stages and check with an L1 plug gauge (or, in a club shop, the actual fitting): it must sit hand-tight flush with the port face within +/- 1 turn (ASME B1.20.1 gauging). Do not run the tap to its shoulder: that gives a port the fitting screws into by hand until it bottoms and never seals. 4) Tap drills: tap_drill is the common UNREAMED size; tap_drill_reamed is the smaller drill for drill-then-taper-ream practice and must not be used without the reamer. Charts differ for 1/8 NPT (R vs 11/32) and 1/16 NPT; see tap_drill_alternatives / disputed. tap_drill_metric_nearest is recall for shops with only metric drills. 5) Depths: min_tapped_depth (L2 + 2p) is a rule of thumb for the full-thread depth of a BLIND port; the same number is the minimum material thickness along the axis at a THROUGH port (min_boss_height_through_port). A through port in a thin end cap still needs this check. blind_drill_depth_full_dia adds the tap's 3.5-thread chamfer lead; blind_drill_depth_to_point adds the 118 deg drill point. Floor material under a blind pocket port is measured from the drill point, and its minimum is a pressure/strength question outside this table. 6) Engagement: hand-tight is L1; wrench-tight adds about L3 (3 threads). Design the port thread length to L2 (full-form threads carry the seal); L1 + L3 (= L5) is within ~0.01 in of L2 but is not the design value. A port shallower than L2 bottoms the fitting before it seals. Turns past finger tight (recall): 1.5-3 in steel/brass, 1-2 in aluminium; more than this is what splits an aluminium boss. NPT is not indefinitely reusable; each re-make drives the fitting deeper. 7) SEALANT. NPT seals by flank interference and needs a sealant (dry seal only with NPTF). For air/water/fuel: PTFE tape (start 1-2 threads back from the end so shreds cannot enter the system) or an anaerobic pipe sealant. FOR OXIDISER (nitrous, LOX, GOX) SERVICE anaerobic thread sealants of the common Loctite 545/567 class are NOT the default and are generally not oxygen-rated; use oxygen-compatible PTFE tape or an oxygen-rated PTFE paste, apply sparingly, and keep tape/paste out of the flow path. 8) BSP CONFUSION. UK/EU/AU shops and fittings use BSPT (R, tapered, 55 deg) and BSPP (G, parallel, 55 deg). 1/4 BSPT is 19 tpi 55 deg vs 1/4 NPT 18 tpi 60 deg; 1/2 and 3/4 share 14 tpi with NPT but the 55 deg flank and different diameters make them NOT interchangeable and NOT sealing when mixed. A generic 'pipe tap drill chart' may be BSP; check the family before drilling. 9) WHY A 1/4 NPT PORT ON A 60 BAR NITROUS TANK IS NORMALLY IN A BOSS: a tapered thread seals by wedging; every turn past hand-tight radially expands the female thread (hoop stress), highest right at the port. A thin tank wall or thin end cap cannot carry that plus the 60 bar pressure load plus bending from a fitting/line, and a thin wall gives less than L2 of thread so the fitting bottoms or leaks. A boss gives (a) full L2 thread depth, (b) surrounding wall (min_boss_od) to react the wedging hoop stress without yielding or cracking (aluminium alloys are especially prone to boss splitting when over-torqued), (c) a flat spot face (port_chamfer_dia / spot face) for the fitting shoulder and wrench (typical_fitting_hex_af across corners must clear). In a welded tank the boss also keeps the tapped thread out of the weld HAZ. For a machined end cap: leave at least min_boss_od of solid material around each port and at least L2 + 2p of thickness, and prefer SAE J1926 / ISO 1179 / ISO 6149 straight-thread O-ring ports over NPT for pressure vessels where you can; they do not stress the boss and seal repeatably. 10) PORT SPACING (recall rule): centre-to-centre spacing between two ports >= (min_boss_od_a + min_boss_od_b)/2; port centre to part edge >= min_boss_od/2; if wrench clearance is larger (fitting across-corners + wrench body), that governs. 11) min_boss_od is a recalled rule of thumb (roughly 1.65-2x pipe OD; see min_boss_od_ratio_to_od) and is NOT from any standard and NOT a checked pressure-vessel minimum. The CAD tool must present it as a rule of thumb, not a verified value. The pressure-boundary calculation (hoop stress, burst margin, thread-wedging stress) is out of the scope of this table and must be done separately for every pressurised port. 12) Confidence: the row-level 'confidence' is the lowest of the standard-derived fields (L1/L2/L4/E/K0 values are recalled from ASME B1.20.1 Table 1 and independently matched to an open-source table, so 'likely'); OD, tpi, pitch, taper and thread angle are fixed values of the standard ('certain' in field_confidence); tap drills are trade consensus ('likely', with disputes listed per row); every column whose description starts with RECALL is 'recall'. Verify L-values against the standard before cutting a flight pressure part. 13) Rows dropped: none; the fitness review found no row too uncertain to cut metal from. Items reviewers asked for that this table does NOT supply: a numeric minimum floor thickness under a blind pocket port (pressure-dependent) and any hoop-stress/burst numbers for bosses (design calculation, not a table value).

structural_changes: renamed thread_height_H_* to thread_height_h_* (standard's h = 0.8p) and added sharp_v_height_H_* (H = 0.866p) so the symbols match ASME B1.20.1

added E0, E1, E2, K0, V, L5 columns and thread-count columns, re-derived from the standard's formulas (E0 = D - (0.05D+1.1)p; E1 = E0 + 0.0625 L1; E2 = E0 + 0.0625 L2; K0 = E0 - h; V = 3.47p; L5 = L2 + L3), all cross-checked against recalled Table 1 values and BOSL2 L4
L4 column description now states L4 = L2 + V, not L2 + L3; v_vanish column added so the relation is checkable
added reamed tap-drill column, tap_drill_alternatives text, per-row 'disputed' for 1/16 and 1/8 tap drills, and metric nearest-drill text (recall)

added gauge_check (L1 plug flush +/-1 turn), blind drill depths (full-dia and to-point), min boss height for through ports, port chamfer dia, typical fitting hex AF (all recall/rule-of-thumb, labelled)
added is_nps_pipe_size and a remark on 1/16 NPT being a fitting-only thread
min_boss_od wording widened to 1.65-2x and min_boss_od_ratio_to_od added (3/8 and 3/4 rows are 1.67x)
min_tapped_depth_mm relabelled as a RECALL rule of thumb, not 'derived from the standard'
od_in description corrected: D is pipe OD / nominal major diameter, not a fit dimension at the gauge plane
added field_confidence map; row-level confidence documented as applying to standard-derived fields only
